data.one_liner: Drop-in wrapper for SharedPreferences with type safety and zero boilerplate.
data.what_it_does: Makes local key-value persistence simpler by allowing developers to define variables once with typed Prf objects and use them anywhere with get() and set(). It supports primitives, enums, lists, and JSON without manual string key management.
use_when: You want a cleaner, type-safe alternative to raw SharedPreferences.
You want to avoid managing string keys and casting values manually across the app.
avoid_when: You need complex relational queries or high-performance local databases.
You require secure encryption out of the box for sensitive data.
strengths: Zero boilerplate with typed variable definitions.
Supports 20+ built-in types, enums, and JSON models seamlessly.
weaknesses: Relies underneath on SharedPreferences, making it unsuited for large relational datasets.
data.setup_notes: No native platform setup required beyond adding the package to pubspec.yaml.

alternatives.name: shared_preferences
alternatives.why_pick_it: You want the official raw package without third-party abstractions.

alternatives.name: flutter_secure_storage
alternatives.why_pick_it: You need encrypted local storage for sensitive tokens or credentials.

alternatives.name: sqflite
alternatives.why_pick_it: You need a full relational SQL database instead of simple key-value storage.
